candidates.exact_span: reports required by Part III.D. to the EPA and copies to NMED as required (See Part III.D.IV of the permit). Reports shall be submitted monthly.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines which recurring DMR/reporting submissions are required and at what frequency; different readings of Part III.D. cross-references or monthly cadence change which FY2025 monitoring expectations are in force and whether absent reports are missing required evidence versus not applicable.

candidates.exact_span: Reporting periods shall end on the last day of each month.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets the calendar boundaries for monthly monitoring/reporting periods; a different period-end interpretation changes which measurements roll into which monthly average or reporting interval for limit comparison and obligation tracking.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee is required to submit regular monthly reports no later than the 15th day of the month.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a due-date obligation for monthly reports; whether a report is late, missing, or not yet due affects whether monitoring was required and how missing-evidence cases should be classified in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The annual sludge report required in Part IV of the permit is due on February 19 of each year and covers the previous calendar year from January 1 through December 31.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a distinct annual sludge-reporting obligation with a fixed coverage window; interpretation of Part IV linkage, due date, and calendar-year scope changes which FY2025 sludge monitoring expectations apply and whether absent sludge data is a documented no-data state or missing required evidence.

candidates.exact_span: If any 30 day average, monthly average, 7 day average, weekly average, or daily maximum value exceeds the effluent limitations specified in Part I.A, the permittee shall report the excursion in accordance with the requirements of Part III.D.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies which reported statistic types (30-day, monthly, 7-day, weekly, daily maximum) are compared against Part I.A limits and trigger excursion reporting; different readings of which average applies to which parameter change exceedance determinations and downstream reporting obligations.

candidates.exact_span: Any 30 day average, monthly average, 7 day average, weekly average, or daily maximum value reported in the required Discharge Monitoring Report which is in excess of the effluent limitation specified in Part I.A shall constitute evidence of violation of such effluent limitation and of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines when a reported DMR value counts as evidence of limit exceedance/violation; interpretation of which averaging basis is enforceable for a given parameter directly changes whether a measurement is treated as exceeding an applicable numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span: Other measurements of oxygen demand (e.g., TOC and COD) may be substituted for five day Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD5) or for five day Carbonaceous Biochemical Oxygen Demand (CBOD5), as applicable, where the permittee can demonstrate long term correlation of the method with BOD5 or CBOD5 values, as applicable. Details of the correlation procedures used must be submitted and prior approval granted by the permitting authority for this procedure to be acceptable. Data reported must also include evidence to show that the proper correlation continues to exist after approval.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Allows alternative oxygen-demand parameters in place of BOD5/CBOD5 only under demonstrated correlation and prior approval; whether substitution is valid changes which numeric limit applies to reported values and whether substitute monitoring satisfies the underlying monitoring requirement.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall report all overflows with the Discharge Monitoring Report submittal. These reports shall be summarized and reported in tabular format. The summaries shall include: the date, time, duration, location, estimated volume, and cause of the overflow; observed environmental impacts from the overflow; actions taken to address the overflow; and ultimate discharge location if not contained (e.g., storm sewer system, ditch, tributary).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes overflow reporting content and timing tied to DMR submittals; interpretation of what counts as an overflow event or required tabular fields changes whether overflow monitoring/reporting was required in FY2025 and how incomplete overflow records are classified.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall report any noncompliance which may endanger health or the environment. Notification shall be made to the EPA at the following e-mail address: R6_NPDES_Reporting@epa.gov, as soon as possible, but within 24 hours from the time the permittee becomes aware of the circumstance.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a conditional 24-hour notification obligation keyed to noncompliance that may endanger health or the environment; different interpretations of the endangerment threshold or awareness timing change which events trigger required reporting and whether absent notifications indicate missing required evidence.
